name: Social Capital Lab
summary: The lab's public home for measures of social capital built from Facebook friendship networks: how connected people are across geography (SCI), gender (CGFR) and class (Economic Connectedness). Mike co-founded the Social Capital Lab at Facebook and is a co-author on the SCI and CGFR releases.
question: How connected are people across geography, gender, and class? What drives differences in these measures of social capital? What outcomes are associated with them?

measures.name: Social Connectedness Index (SCI)
measures.definition: A globally comparable measure of the relative probability that Facebook users in two locations are friends. Scaled for the size of the two populations; compare within one release and geographic level, never as a count or probability.

tools.name: Interactive Explorer
tools.answers: Where is this country or region most connected? Click a place on a globe and see its strongest ties.

tools.name: Map Maker
tools.answers: Make a publication-quality SCI map with chosen geography, colors, breaks and titles; export as image or video.

tools.name: Local Network Share
tools.answers: Pick a distance and color every place by the estimated share of its friendship network that lives within it.

tools.name: Connected Communities
tools.answers: Group the places in a country or region into a chosen number of clusters by how tightly they are connected.

data.notes: Country table is small; subnational tables run to hundreds of megabytes. Use the download for subnational work; this MCP serves the country level through query_social_connections.

citations: Johnston, D., Kuchler, T., Kulkarni, M., & Stroebel, J. (2026). The Social Connectedness Index: A Large-Scale Dataset of Social Ties Across Geographic Locations. Data in Brief, 67, 112905. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2026.112905

Bailey, M., Cao, R., Kuchler, T., Stroebel, J., & Wong, A. (2018). Social Connectedness: Measurement, Determinants, and Effects. Journal of Economic Perspectives, 32(3), 259-280. https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.32.3.259

measures.name: Cross-Gender Friending Ratio (CGFR)
measures.definition: For a location, the share of women among men's friends divided by the share of women among women's friends, computed over each user's top-n closest friends. A value of 1 means men and women form equal shares of their ties with women; lower values mean more gender-segregated networks. Differential-privacy noise is added and small cells are dropped.
findings: Across countries, CGFR correlates strongly with gender differences in labor force participation.
Within countries, people from areas with higher CGFR are typically more supportive of equal treatment of men and women.
County-level differences in CGFR line up with demographic and socioeconomic patterns across the United States.

tools.name: Interactive Explorer
tools.answers: Where are cross-gender friendship networks more or less separated? Click a country or region on a globe.

data.notes: Static release; no regular updates planned. This MCP serves the country and US county tables through query_cross_gender_ties.

citations: Bailey, M., Johnston, D., Kuchler, T., Kumar, A., & Stroebel, J. (2025). Cross-Gender Social Ties around the World. AEA Papers and Proceedings, 115, 132-138. https://doi.org/10.1257/pandp.20251032

measures.name: Economic Connectedness (EC)
measures.definition: A measure of cross-class friendship networks by place: the share of high-socioeconomic-status friends among low-SES people, normalized. The US release is the Social Capital Atlas; a worldwide release is in preparation.
measures.status: Coming soon on social-connectedness.org as of 2026-09-23. The US Social Capital Atlas is available now.

tools.name: Social Capital Atlas (US)
tools.answers: Economic connectedness, cohesiveness and civic engagement for US counties, ZIPs, colleges and high schools.

data.notes: This MCP serves the US Atlas through query_social_capital.
